Instrument (EN): Body Uneasiness Test, Part A — Dutch translated clinical/community validation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Five domains: Weight Phobia; Body Image Concerns; Avoidance; Compulsive Self-Monitoring; Depersonalization. Global Severity Index is an averaged item score.
Research provenance: van Uffelen LM, de Beurs E, Melisse B. J Clin Psychol 2026-04-03; DOI 10.1002/jclp.70143. Dutch forward/back translation; study clinical self-reported eating-disorder N448 and community N223 (eligible); complete-case N434 and N217 respectively for all instruments; BUT-A and BUT-B use SAME participants. 5-factor CFA; AUC range .77–.88 for test family, test-retest BUT-A ICC .54 (moderate).
DB locales: not_registered in published Supabase; same BUT family as separately indexed Dutch Part B. Do not double count participants.
EN form: Original source English form discussed; original is not newly EN translated or validated in the NL study.
RU form: No independently validated RU respondent version verified from this study.
ES form: No ES respondent edition psychometric validation established by this study.
Other translations: NL-NL: forward/back-translated Dutch participant form in two Dutch cohorts; distinguish from Dutch BUT-B Part B. No additional translations proven.
Target population: Self-reported eating-disorder pathology participants N448 and community participants N223, age >=16, Netherlands; analyses use smaller complete-case sizes N434/N217. Clinical diagnoses not interview-confirmed.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Commercial digital use of original BUT items, Dutch adapted form, automated scores, translated content and clinical cutoffs NOT licensed. Obtain permission from original and Dutch adaptation rights holders and professional review; article open access is NOT automatically commercial test-use permission.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. Dutch A and B use same samples and one translation study, not independent replication. Moderate one-week test-retest for BUT-A and limited construct separation; do not implement screening cutoffs or test delivery.

Instrument (EN): Body Uneasiness Test, Part B — Dutch translated body-region concerns form
Scales / measured domains (EN): Eight body-region discomfort subfactors (BUT-B I–VIII); Positive Symptom Total (count endorsed items), Positive Symptom Distress Index (average endorsed severity). Not same five dimensions as BUT-A.
Research provenance: van Uffelen LM et al. J Clin Psychol 2026-04-03, DOI 10.1002/jclp.70143; same original Dutch translation and N448 self-reported eating pathology + N223 community samples as BUT-A; complete-case N434+217; B 8-factor structure evaluated, certain B subscales reliability weak (e.g. factor VII 2 items), low item-rest for facial-hair items.
DB locales: not_registered; separate 37-item PART of BUT, not independent questionnaire family from Part A or independent validation sample.
EN form: Original English part exists; this paper does not validate an EN translation.
RU form: RU respondent B edition not verified.
ES form: ES respondent B edition not verified.
Other translations: NL-NL: Dutch respondent translation evaluated with same N as BUT-A; no other language evidence from article.
Target population: Participants age >=16 in Netherlands; eating pathology cohort N448 plus community N223 (analysis complete cases 434+217). Note some body parts/face-hair questions may be inapplicable to some people.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: No independent license for digital commercial use of 37 translated item statements, body-part distress scoring, clinical cutoffs or integration with identifiable health data. Both BUT family and translated rights require review.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. BUT-B is same-paper supplementary part, eight factors have unequal quality, validity and relevance by body part. Do not count as second validation population or activate scoring.

Instrument (EN): Attune & Stimulate Checklist — observational behavior catalogue for profound intellectual disabilities
Question count: 92 behavioural item OPTIONS across 13 categories; NOT 92 self-report questions
Scales / measured domains (EN): 13 observed-body/behavior groupings: Actions, Sounds, Position, Whole/Upper/Lower Body, Arms, Hands, Feet, Head, Eyes, Nose, Mouth. Observed arousal-valence on ordinal -3 to +3; percentages by rating; multiple scores per observed option.
Research provenance: Doodeman TWM, Schuengel C, Sterkenburg PS, J Appl Res Intellect Disabil 2026-01-28 DOI 10.1111/jar.70170. Trained-observer video study N102 adults with severe/profound intellectual disabilities (ages 18–81), control/physiology N55 SUBSET. ICC interrater .77–.83, retest .70–.81, but observed arousal did not correlate with skin conductance.
DB locales: not_registered; OBSERVATION instrument, not client self-completed digital assessment. 149/234 published DB read-only.
EN form: English journal article is NOT independent EN observer-checklist language validation.
Other translations: Dutch institutional context (NL) but original observer form's exact language NOT independently confirmed; never claim validated NL-NL translation from publication setting.
Target population: Adults 18–81 with severe to profound intellectual disabilities, 102 video-recorded people in Dutch care settings; observation conducted by trained professionals.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Written rights for commercial distribution of 92 behavioural options, scoring rubric and trainer material NOT confirmed. Separate professional observer training, accessibility, safeguarding, data and video consent are essential.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY / OBSERVER_RATED. 92 codes are not survey question count. Four groups of emotional arousal differ from independent self-report scales. Physiological-arousal association absent; never use as autonomous website quiz.

Research provenance: Cruz M, Grilo A, Custódio S, Dores AR, Silva C, Alves P; Acta Psychologica 263 (2026) 106272, published 2026-01-25; DOI 10.1016/j.actpsy.2026.106272. Pilot N106 Portuguese psychologists rated draft 57 items, factor extraction/refinement resulted in 43 final items; reported EFA/CFA from SAME pilot, NOT independent validation.
DB locales: not_registered in published Supabase; original Portuguese-specific scale, distinct from Perth Empathy Scale and Therapist Empathy Scale.
EN form: English-language publication abstract alone does not prove validated English participant version.
RU form: No validated RU respondent adaptation evidenced.
ES form: No validated ES respondent adaptation evidenced.
Other translations: PT-PT: developed and pilot-tested for Portuguese psychologists. Final 43-item independent administration not separately demonstrated in N106 pilot.
Target population: 106 Portuguese practising psychologists in pilot of original Portuguese-speaking professional self-evaluation; no independent new validation N.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Repository text published under CC BY-NC-ND metadata (noncommercial, no derivatives); no independently documented commercial digital right for complete final 43-item form, derivatives, translation or software scoring. Seek written license from author/rightsholder.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED / PILOT ONLY. Same 106 rated initial 57; final 43 not independently validated or normed. Self-report professional empathy is not diagnostic or independent clinical competence verification.

Instrument (EN): Double Awareness Scale — original Canadian English palliative oncology form
Scales / measured domains (EN): Two subscales: Life Engagement (21) and Death Contemplation (13); balance between engagement with life and realistic contemplation of death in advanced cancer.
Research provenance: Miljanovski M et al. Psycho-Oncology published 2026-04-17 DOI 10.1002/pon.70445; N197 evaluable adult advanced-cancer outpatients at Canadian palliative care clinic; 41-item initial pool EFA eliminated 7, final 34 two factors, alpha .92 and .87; preliminary convergent evidence, some hypothesized relations not observed. Article appendix contains 34 items, not commercial licence.
DB locales: not_registered; acronym DAS may overlap unrelated scales, stable key distinct. No published site palliative double-awareness assessment.
EN form: Original English-speaking Canadian respondents used English form; no independently translated EN questionnaire (original).
RU form: No independently validated RU participant translation.
ES form: No ES respondent questionnaire psychometric study from this primary paper.
Other translations: EN-CA ORIGINAL; not a newly translated English-language edition; no additional independent-language translations confirmed.
Target population: 197 adults with advanced cancer under ambulatory palliative care in Toronto, Canada; diagnosis-specific high-sensitivity clinical context.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Explicit written permission required to host 34 questionnaire items, score or produce interpretations on commercial SaaS despite OA paper appendix. Ethical supervision, advanced-disease consent/privacy, appropriate distress and crisis safeguards required.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. Palliative cohort, preliminary single-site factorial validity only, not universal double-awareness norm. 41 initial items not final score. Never diagnose or market unsupervised web-based mortality contemplation.

Instrument (EN): Narrative Identity Self-Evaluation Scale — Polish respondent adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Autobiographical Reasoning (5); Desire for Narrative Structure (5); Positive Themes (5); Narrative Identity Disturbances (5); no assumption of one diagnostic total score.
Research provenance: Soroko E, Kleka P, Martyńska M, Janowicz K; Current Psychology 45 article1392, published 2026-08-24, DOI 10.1007/s12144-026-09918-5. Translated/adapted Polish version studied N336 Polish adults 18–75; original four-factor model had incomplete fit (CFI .881; RMSEA .069; SRMR .09); post-hoc modified model improved CFI .921, RMSEA .057; factor AVE only .364–.446 (<.50); caution on construct equivalence.
DB locales: not_registered; avoid conflating Narrative Identity Self-Evaluation Scale with broader narrative identity/attachment tests.
EN form: Original NISE elsewhere may exist English; this study does not newly validate EN adaptation.
RU form: No independently validated RU translation from the Poland source.
ES form: No ES respondent-version validation from this source.
Other translations: PL-PL Polish participant version translated and psychometrically studied, but prespecified CFA / convergent validity limitations; do not claim strong unqualified clinical validation.
Target population: 336 adults in Poland aged 18–75, predominantly young adults, nonrepresentative convenience sample; correlations with mental-health scales are not clinical cutoffs.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Current Psychology article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial/no derivatives); original NISE and Polish translated items require written permission for commercial SaaS copy, adaptation, automated scoring; no clearance.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Initial factorial fit insufficient; modified CFA exploratory/post-hoc, convergent AVE below .5. No clinical diagnosis, norms, item delivery or automatic scoring.
